## Zoning & Development Analysis — 3400 N Central Park Ave (PIN 13233160400000)

*Parcel resolution: **authoritative** — the PIN was matched directly from Cook County's address records, so all parcel-level data below applies to this specific lot.*

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3 (Residential Single-Unit – Detached House)**. [4] describes RS districts as intended primarily to accommodate detached houses on individual lots, with three sub-districts (RS1, RS2, RS3) differentiated mainly by minimum lot area and FAR. You can verify the current zoning designation on the official Chicago Zoning Map: [https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning)

> **Note:** The property records show this is a 2-story, 5-unit masonry building built in 1927 — a pre-existing nonconforming use relative to the RS-3 district, which currently permits single-unit detached houses as its primary use.

---

### 2. Could You Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Possibly — but only under a specific condition.** Under [2], in an RS-3 district the minimum lot area per dwelling unit may be reduced to 1,500 sq ft *when 60% or more of the zoning lots fronting on the same side of the street between the two nearest intersecting streets have been lawfully improved with buildings containing more than one dwelling unit* — or when the property falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundaries defined by §17-7-0591. This exemption only allows establishment of a **two-unit building** (not larger). Without that block-level condition being met, RS-3 limits development to a single-unit detached house. You would need to verify the block composition through the Zoning Map or by contacting the Department of Planning and Development.

---

### 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards (RS-3)

The context does not include the full RS-3 zone definition text (the `zone_definition` field was not returned), so I cannot state precise FAR, maximum height, or setback figures with certainty from the retrieved code. What can be confirmed:

- **Minimum lot area per unit:** Under [2], the RS-3 standard applies; the 1,500 sq ft/unit reduced minimum applies only under the two-flat block-condition described above.
- **Other factors limiting density:** [2] explicitly notes that *off-street parking, height limits, dwelling unit sizes, and lot configuration may work to limit density more than the minimum lot area standards alone.*
- **FAR, maximum height, and setbacks:** These are defined in §17-2-0400 through §17-2-0500 of the Zoning Ordinance, which were not retrieved in this query. **I cannot state those figures** — they should be verified directly in the Municipal Code or via the Chicago Zoning Map.

To verify: Search §17-2-0400 (Bulk and Intensity Standards for RS districts) at [Chicago Municipal Code](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/chicago/latest/chicago_il/0-0-0-2624220).

---

### 4. Overlays and Special Designations

The following apply to this parcel:

- **Special District** — This parcel falls within a Special District designation. The specific nature and restrictions of this district were not detailed in the retrieved data; contact the Department of Planning and Development for specifics.
- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — The parcel is within a CTA Transit-Oriented Development overlay, reflecting its proximity (0.25 miles) to the Addison Blue Line station. See §17-10-0102-B for parking implications (discussed in section 5).
- **ADU Eligible Area** — This parcel is within an Additional Dwelling Unit–Allowed RS Area [1], making it eligible for conversion units and/or coach houses under the ADU program (discussed in section 6).
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any qualifying residential development may be subject to affordability requirements. The Avondale community area has 6 ARO-related affordable housing projects totaling 76 units, including Hairpin Lofts (25 units at 3414 W. Diversey Ave.), Milwaukee Ave. Apts. (32 units of supportive housing at 3060 N. Milwaukee Ave.), and The Field's Lofts (12 units at 4000 W. Diversey Ave.).
- **No Planned Development** — Not in a Planned Development.
- **No Landmark/Historic Designation** — Not in a landmark or historic district; not individually landmarked; not on the National Register.
- **No Lakefront Protection, No PMD, No SSA.**
- **Flood Zone X** — FEMA designation "Area of Minimal Flood Hazard." This is **not** a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not federally required.
- **Brownfield sites nearby** — Two EPA-listed brownfield properties are in the broader area: *BNSF Little Village Paseo Segment 1* (EPA ID 110071982538) and *BNSF Little Village Paseo Segment 2* (EPA ID 110071982539). These are not on this parcel, but environmental due diligence may be advisable for any ground-disturbing work.

---

### 5. Parking Requirements and Transit-Related Reduction

Under [5] (§17-10-0601), in RS districts required off-street parking for residential uses must be located on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served, and off-street parking is prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line (except when accessed by a permitted driveway).

**Transit-served parking relief:** Because this parcel is within the CTA TOD overlay (0.25 miles from Addison Blue Line), it qualifies for a parking minimum reduction of **up to 100%** under §17-10-0102-B — meaning parking minimums could potentially be waived entirely. However, **no density, FAR, or height bonus applies** in RS-3; those transit-served bonuses apply only in dash-3 districts (e.g., B1-3, B2-3, C1-3, etc.), not in RS-3.

The parcel currently has a 3-car garage noted in property records.

---

### 6. Coach House / Additional Dwelling Units (ADUs)

**Yes, this parcel is eligible** — it falls within an ADU-Allowed RS Area [1]. The purpose of these areas is to allow organic, contextual growth through conversion units and coach houses to create unsubsidized affordable housing, enable multi-generational living, or provide owners additional revenue [1].

Key conditions and limits under [3] (§17-9-0200):

- A new coach house building permit in an RS-designated lot **may not be issued unless it complies with** [1] (§17-7-0570).
- Coach houses **may not exceed 22 feet in building height** [3].
- Rooftop features may not exceed 22 feet above grade [3].
- At least **3 feet of unobstructed open space** must be provided between the coach house and at least one side property line for the full length of the building wall (except where a side property line abuts an alley or street) [3].
- Coach houses are limited to the **rear portion of the lot** (in B/C districts: rear 30 feet — the RS-specific siting rules are in §17-7-0570, which should be consulted directly) [3].
- Coach houses **may be established without accessory parking** to serve the coach house itself [3].
- Accessory parking for the principal building may be reduced or waived via administrative adjustment [3].
- Specific limitations on conversion units or coach house numbers may be set by §17-7-0573 and §17-7-0574 for this particular ADU area [1] — those details were not fully retrieved.

**Enforcement** of the ADU pre-certification process is handled by the **Department of Housing** under §2-44-106(g) [1]. Start there for the pre-certification application.
